_why: The SOURCE commits of a squash merge stop being reachable once the branch is deleted: they live on no ref that a CI checkout fetches. Captured here so the composer can be driven without them. The EXPECTED output is NOT stored - it is read live from the squash commit on main, which anchors these rows: edit a body here and the byte comparison stops matching.

cases.title: PHASE-1.2c FINAL: a withdrawn claim, the TTL boundary, and the sixth refusal row

commits.subject: PHASE-1.2c FINAL: a withdrawn claim, the TTL boundary, and the sixth refusal row
commits.body:
Most of what this sprint asked for landed in #101 and is verified here rather
than rebuilt. What was genuinely missing was smaller and more specific, and two
of the three findings are corrections to my own work.

THE WITHDRAWN CLAIM. execution/pending.py's module docstring said "pinning
removes re-resolution from the approval path" in the first clause of the
approval order, while step 3 of the same list — and the code — re-resolved.
Approval runs chain binding, then the pinned policy, then restore_persisted,
which re-resolves the selected policy for the concrete action exactly as at
hold time. The claim is withdrawn in place and what pinning does NOT do is now
stated, because the same assumption has now arrived twice from outside: a path
that trusted the stored requirements instead of re-resolving would reintroduce
R1 one layer down, with the JSON column as the new forgeable input.
Documentation only, and proven so rather than asserted: the module's AST with
docstrings stripped is identical across the change. The Hearth digest is
re-sanctioned with that reason beside it.

THE TTL. Its semantics were spread across three method docstrings and a
predicate. Now written once, in the module and in docs/operations.md: evaluated
at BOTH decision time and by the sweep, boundary INCLUSIVE
(elapsed >= ttl_seconds), and a hold that has lapsed but not been swept still
reads "pending" while being unapprovable — the decision-time guard, not the
sweep, is the control. That last state had no test and the boundary had none
either; every existing case jumped from a 100-second TTL to 200 seconds, which
proves a guard exists and says nothing about where it fires. Two tests added:
one second short approves, exactly on it does not; and a lapsed-unswept hold
reads pending, refuses approval, and records the transition itself. Probed
through the worktree runner: making the comparison exclusive reddens the
boundary test and nothing else; removing the decision-time guard reddens three.

THE SIXTH REFUSAL ROW. Five of the six reasons in the closed coverage
vocabulary had a submission proving what they RECORD; coverage.ambiguous was
exercised only against validate_coverage's return value, so nothing said what
an ambiguous refusal writes to a row. It now has a refusing row of its own, and
a test fails if a seventh reason is added without one.

THE `edited` WINDOW. ci.yml's bare pull_request trigger does not fire on
`edited`, so a body rewritten after the last check was unguarded; #101's body
was edited twice after its last passing check (both clean). It cannot be fixed
in ci.yml — that trigger is allowlisted bare on purpose, and event types are
per-workflow — so the check also lives in a second workflow that runs the
checker alone in seconds. Its trigger list is allowlisted too.

MEASURED, and refusing three presuppositions in the brief:
- The type gate went 290 -> 304 this sprint, not 288 -> 304; 304 is
  src + scripts + tests, and the delta is exactly the 14 Python files the
  sprint added.
- The `edited` gap is real but is NOT how a banned token reached main. The
  squash message is composed from the five branch COMMIT messages, with a
  co-authorship trailer appended by GitHub after every pre-merge check has
  passed. G13, with the four options and a recommendation, none taken.
- History re-swept after the merge: main 86 commits / 75 carrying a term; all
  refs 310 / 111. It grew by exactly one commit and one trailer. No rewrite
  executed.

Stale records corrected: a G12 line that said 302 -> 303 while the gate said
304, a withdrawn-claim docstring that read as present tense, and a README
claiming 385 passed / 2 skipped against 2436 / 23.

Observed: 2436 passed, 23 skipped; type gate 304 files; skip manifest clean;
hygiene clean; record mutations 6 / 15 (14 -> 15 for the new parametrisation);
Checkpoint B 6 / 7 unchanged, including hold-admission-check-removed, which is
R3's reproduction.
commits.author: DriivAIDev <will@driivai.com>

cases.title: PHASE-1.2c: refuse banned tokens by construction, three platform channels, the pinned authorization record, and docs/OPEN-GAPS.md

commits.subject: PHASE-1.2c: refuse banned tokens by construction, three platform channels, the pinned authorization record, and docs/OPEN-GAPS.md
commits.body:
===== BLOCKS 1-2 =====

1.1 BANNED TOKENS IN HISTORY — measured before building anything. #100's
squash-merge commit af93238 carries the assistant-session trailer twice and a
co-authorship trailer once. The trailer came from MY branch commits (b0bfaba,
9b9fcdf): I wrote it, contrary to the standing no-trailers rule, and the
squash copied the body. The same is true of #87, #88, #89, #97, #98 and #99.
The harness also set the vendor's no-reply address as the COMMITTER identity
on every branch commit; two remote branches still carry it.

History sweep, scripts/check_message_hygiene.py --history:
  origin/main   85 commits, 74 carrying a term (co-authorship 74 sites,
                vendor name 8, vendor domain 1)
  all refs     304 commits, 110 carrying a term (88 / 40 / 12)
The co-authorship line is written by GitHub's squash merge for any commit
author who is not the merging account — 74 of the 85 commits on main.

The control is now a refusal, not a strip: the same checker over commit
messages, author and committer identities, and PR title/body — as commit-msg
and pre-push hooks (scripts/install_git_hooks.py, per clone) and in CI on
every pull request and on every push to main. Observed: the commit-msg hook
refuses a message carrying the trailer (exit 1) and passes a clean one. Named
limit: the squash commit is created after CI has passed and no pre-merge check
can refuse it; the main-push check detects it loudly; what stops it at the
source is the repository's squash-message setting, outside this tree.

1.2 BRANCH RESURRECTION. pre-push refuses a push to a branch whose remote ref
is absent when the branch has an upstream configured — the one local fact that
separates a re-push of a merged-and-deleted branch from a first push. Observed
refusing DriivAIDev/phase-1-2c-block1-r2-verdict. The stale codex branch's
deletion is refused by the git proxy here (HTTP 403); it needs the UI.

1.3 SKIP SET. Measured locally under the CI environment on 3.10, 3.11 and
3.12: the same 23 skips by name on all three (14 live-database proofs that
run in the dedicated PostgreSQL step, 8 real-container opt-ins, 1 real-container
test skipping for want of a daemon). Pinned in tests/conformance/skip_manifest.txt
and checked by name in CI on every version. The daemon entry is left to the
first CI run to decide; ubuntu-latest ships one. Measured on the way: a venv
under /tmp cannot run this suite at all — the namespace sandbox hides /tmp —
100 failures and 12 errors on both 3.10 and 3.12 until the venvs moved to /opt.

2.1 / 2.2 PLATFORM GATE. Three channels, each keyed on a TYPE: the refusal
RAISED (UnsupportedPlatform, _PlatformUnsupported inside _OwnershipUnavailable),
RETURNED as a MigrationResult / ReconciliationResult carrying the new typed
platform_unsupported field, or RAISED IN A WORKER THREAD, where the test then
waits on an event never set and its own traceback carries no marker. Under the
darwin simulation over tests/chokepoint (912 tests):
  before this change  792 pass, 80 converted, 22 platform/database skips, 18 FAIL
  after               792 pass, 80 + 17 + 1 converted, 22 skips, 0 FAIL
The 18 were 17 assertion failures whose text quoted the result's repr — the
population the first, string-matching gate converted as if they were platform
refusals — plus one thread test. One pytester sub-session per channel shows
PROM_REQUIRE_LINUX=1 firing: skipped without the flag, failed with it, and a
real misconfiguration converted on neither. Refused presupposition: the
returned channel's typed origin is the guard's own _PlatformUnsupported (its
flock-semantics check) or the opened-store probe's UnsupportedPlatform, not
SubstrateReport.platform_unsupported read directly — on that path the
construction-time report was a stub. The result's field is derived from those
types, never from prose.

2.3 ONE SOURCE. PROM_CI_PG_DB/_USER/_PASSWORD live once, in jobs.build.env;
the service container and the live-database step read them by expression and
the health check reads the container's own environment; each literal appears
exactly once (tests/conformance/test_ci_single_source.py). GitHub's context
table confirms the env context is available to services.<id>.env; the live
step in CI is what proves the expression resolved.

2.4 MATRIX. _ROW_KIND pins the state-to-row mapping of the ten-row swarm fault
matrix: eight rows refused before the gate (decision None), one refused at
the gate (returns FAIL — an authoritative FAIL the gate blocks), one legitimate
execution (the positive control). The test used to derive the kind from the
label's spelling; a rule over a string. Every row must be mapped.

ALSO, MEASURED. scripts/mutation_worktree.py ran the worktree's tests against
the PRIMARY tree's package: the editable install's finder resolved the package
to the primary src, so a mutation applied in the worktree reddened nothing
(0 red for a bank.py mutation that reddens 10 in memory). It now puts the
worktree's src first on PYTHONPATH, copies untracked files under include_dirty,
and a planted-mutation test requires the red. And the stdlib-floor guard's
docstring claimed the 25 first-party import errors under a strict type gate
need forbidden per-module sections; measured, widening mypy_path resolves all
25 with no section at all. Claim withdrawn there; the guard's two scope limits
(third-party resolvability, symbol-level additions) are passing tests.

R7: the mint sweep resolves a plain alias assignment (_m = mint), with a
planted control.

===== TASK 5/6 AND BLOCK 0 =====

THE RECORD (TASK 6, the approved schema). Every hold persists a versioned
record — snapshot digest, attempt, policy id/digest/VERSION, the requirements
the selected policy RESOLVED, and the coverage report: which implementation
answered each requirement, which could not, which row refused — and every
executions row carries the record it was decided under (the hold's PINNED
record for human-approved and retried executions; blocked and unavailable rows
name the coverage row that refused). New columns executions.authorization and
pending_actions.invalidated_at / invalidated_reason, additive, ensured on open.
Every value is read off the seam's own re-resolution and the bank's own
report, never off anything a caller supplied.

Dropped from the approved schema, and said so: policy_epoch. It had no source
independent of policy_digest — the supplier hands over a policy VALUE and
nothing else — so it would have been a field that records nothing. The
rotation marker is policy_digest; policy_version is its human handle.

(a) TAMPER EVIDENCE. The record is appended to the audit chain at hold time
under the hold's identity; approval requires the row to equal its entry on a
chain that verifies. Shown: an altered pinned requirement set is refused
("does not match its tamper-evident chain entry"), the chain still valid and
the hold left pending; row and entry altered together break the chain and are
refused; row, entry AND every later hash rewritten is NOT detected without an
anchor and IS detected (BROKEN) with one — the limit as a passing test, both
halves asserted. Refused presupposition: pinning does NOT remove re-resolution
from the approval path here. Re-resolve-don't-re-digest is Checkpoint B's
load-bearing move and removing it would reintroduce R1 exactly; pinning adds
the chain check and the rotation refusal IN FRONT of the same re-resolution.
So the lying record in the undetected case misleads a reviewer and authorizes
nothing extra (a relabelled hold after a rotation is still refused by the
seam, because the assessment's digest commits to the old requirements). The
record's integrity is the asset; the anchor is what protects it.

(b) THREAT MODEL. docs/threat-model.md §3.6: write access to pending_actions
is in scope for detection and out of scope for prevention, inheriting §3's
anchor residual. Doctrine #9 re-sweep: execution-descriptor.md §6/§11 no
longer say approval re-validates "against the currently selected policy";
R5/R6/R7 are recorded as closed there rather than deleted; observability.md,
operations.md and pre-disclosure-audit.md (M2 re-measured: eight commits, not
one) corrected.

(c) THE REFUSING PATH EXERCISES COVERAGE. Coverage runs to completion on both
sides: satisfied with an unavailable sibling recorded, and refused by a real
coverage row — invalid_evidence (the result names one implementation and the
evidence another, the row the positional-Evidence defect hid behind),
abstained, incomplete, advisory_only (each an unavailable row naming the
reason) and unsatisfactory (a FAIL the gate blocks). An assessment minted
without coverage validation says "recorded: false" rather than presenting an
empty report as a clean one.

TASK 5. hold rejects a caller-constructed GateDecision (unchanged, cited).
Approval compares against the pin first: the row must match its chain entry,
the deployment must still select the pinned policy, and only then is the
record decoded inside the seam and re-resolved. A hold pinned to a superseded
policy is refused as PinnedPolicySuperseded — a distinct refusal — and voided
(status invalidated, decided_by system:policy-rotation, the flat columns set),
whether the new policy is stricter or weaker; a second approval is refused as
decided and the hold no longer lists as pending. Rotation invalidates the
backlog explicitly (invalidate_superseded_holds), leaving holds created under
the new policy untouched and approvable — the control inside the negative. A
retry after a rotation is refused and the human's approval record is
untouched. The TTL is unchanged. Positive control first: a legitimate hold
approved under an unrotated policy still executes, and its execution row
carries the pinned record byte for byte.

PROOFS. test_execution_authorization_record.py (15) and test_hold_pinning.py
(7), pinned in ci.yml with zero skips. scripts/phase_1_2c_record_revert_proofs.py:
6 executed mutations — both halves of the chain binding, the pinned-policy
comparison, the invalidation write, the coverage report at minting, the
execution row's record — 6 caught, 14 call-phase failures, pinned. The
Checkpoint-B mutation "hold-policy-re-resolution-removed" is re-expressed as
"hold-pinned-policy-comparison-removed" against the code that now carries the
property; its runner is unchanged at 6 / 7. The 1.2a runner's pin moves 25 ->
26 because the matrix's "returns FAIL" row now asserts the gate was reached,
which the fuse-without-coverage mutation trips; identified by name through
the (now working) mutation worktree. The 1.2b runner's assess mutation is
re-expressed against the two-line tail that mints with the report (7 / 9,
unchanged). The 2d sweep's permitted constructor moves from judge_covered to
_judge_with_coverage, the same construction one function over.

HEARTH. bank.py (assess keeps the coverage report; judge_covered delegates;
judge unchanged, decision surface 240 rows unchanged), core/interfaces.py
(record_execution takes the record; the port gains invalidate_pending_action
and the audit-chain trio), execution/pending.py, execution/controller.py —
re-sanctioned with the reason beside each. Type gate 290 -> 302 files.

docs/OPEN-GAPS.md — the tracker, seeded G1-G11 with measured numbers: the
mypy 25 (and the corrected reason), positional construction 49 wide / 47
sites with the per-class table and #100's blast radius, the stdlib-floor
scope, F10 parked with the scoping-pass boundary, F11 INDETERMINATE on AWS,
banned tokens in history, the skip manifest's one open entry, the platform
gate's three channels and their limits, the record's anchor-bounded tamper
evidence, the simulation as a local instrument, and the stale remote branches.
Where a gap is a limit it is a passing test (test_open_gaps.py ratchets the
positional sites per class; test_stdlib_floor.py carries the scope limits).

commits.subject: pre-push: a branch that tracks origin/main is a first push, not a resurrection
commits.body:
The first version refused this repository's own sprint branch. A branch
created with `git checkout -b X origin/main` carries an upstream — main's —
so "remote ref absent AND an upstream configured" read a first push as a
re-push. Observed on the first push of this branch, which the hook refused.
The rule now requires the upstream to name THIS branch on THIS remote
(branch.X.remote == the remote, branch.X.merge == refs/heads/X), which is
what a branch that was pushed and then deleted under the clone carries and a
fresh branch does not. Re-observed: the merged-and-deleted block-1 branch is
still refused; this branch is allowed.
commits.author: DriivAIDev <will@driivai.com>

commits.subject: OPEN-GAPS G6: the PR-body check observed refusing an injected footer in CI
commits.body:
Recorded from #101's first run: the harness appended a vendor-named footer to
the PR body at creation, and the "Message hygiene" step refused the body
(commits and title passed). The body was stripped by editing the PR. A limit
surfaced with it: the bare pull_request trigger does not fire on `edited`, so
a corrected body is re-checked only on the next push — this commit is that
push. The trigger allowlist refuses filters on purpose; the trade is recorded
in the entry rather than made quietly.
commits.author: DriivAIDev <will@driivai.com>

commits.subject: CI: re-pin the two stale collection counts, and check the pins in the suite
commits.body:
Run 34701799636 refused all three matrix jobs at the PHASE-1.2a step with
('test_policy_enforcement_regression', 20, 19), after a local suite that was
green on three interpreters. Two tests added in this branch moved the
collected counts and the pins in .github/workflows/ci.yml did not follow. The
step's loop stops at the first mismatch, so the second stale pin
(test_no_second_aggregator, 12 against a pinned 11) was read out of the JUnit
file behind it. Twenty-three steps never ran on that commit.

Both pins corrected, with the reason beside each number. The class of miss is
closed rather than noted: tests/conformance/test_ci_collection_pins.py parses
the pins out of the workflow (both shapes it uses — the per-module mapping and
a bare total), collects the files each pinned step runs in one pass, and
compares, in the ordinary suite where the author can see it. Probed directly
rather than assumed: against the tree at 77669ad the guard reports both
mismatches; against the corrected pins it is silent. Its limits are passing
tests — it reads collection, not outcomes, and the set of steps it can read is
itself pinned in both directions.

Type gate 302 -> 303 files. docs/OPEN-GAPS.md G12 records the miss, the
control and the limits; G11's description of the pre-push rule is corrected to
the rule as narrowed in 2991f63.

Observed: 2424 passed, 23 skipped (the same 23 by name, manifest clean); type
gate reports 303 files; every other workflow step replayed locally from a
worktree of 77669ad passes, with the live-database step left to CI.

commits.subject: Skip manifest: two sections, because the set is a property of the tree ON A HOST
commits.body:
The manifest was pinned from a local run and its first CI run refused. It was
right twice. The predicted half: ubuntu-latest ships a container daemon, so
test_real_container_workspace_stays_owner_only_and_still_works RAN there and the
sanction was stale. The unpredicted half, and the finding: that runner is also
unprivileged, so test_another_local_user_cannot_read_or_write_the_workspace
SKIPPED there, where this host runs as root and runs it. Both hosts report
"2424 passed, 23 skipped" — the same count, a different set, which is the exact
blindness the manifest was built to remove.

So an entry now lives in one of two sections. [required] keeps the original
rule: must skip everywhere, an entry that ran is stale and fails. [conditional]
is for a skip that depends on a named host fact, and must carry
`proof: <workflow> :: <step>` naming a step that runs the test under a
PROM_REQUIRE_* flag — the flag that makes a skip a FAILURE there. The checker
resolves the workflow, the step and the flag, and refuses a conditional entry
whose proof does not hold: a sanction with nothing behind it is a hole, not a
sanction. Exactly two entries are conditional, the two that swap.

tests/conformance/test_skip_manifest_guard.py drives the checker over both
recorded host compositions (both must pass), an unsanctioned skip and a stale
required entry (both must fail), and four broken proofs with a fifth that
resolves as the positive control. Named limit, a passing test: a conditional
entry is excused wherever it skips, and the container proof runs nightly and on
sandbox-path pull requests rather than every build.

docs/OPEN-GAPS.md G7 closed with that limit; the workflow step's comment no
longer claims a sanctioned test that ran always fails. Type gate 303 -> 304.

Observed: 2431 passed, 23 skipped; manifest clean, reporting the conditional
entry that ran here; type gate 304 files.
commits.author: DriivAIDev <will@driivai.com>
